name: Pontiac fever

criteria.description: Acute onset of febrile illness within 24-48 hours after exposure
History of recent exposure to aerosolized water sources contaminated with Legionella species
Laboratory evidence of Legionella infection (serology, culture, or PCR)
Spontaneous resolution of symptoms within 2-5 days without antibiotic treatment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Acute febrile illness with exposure history and laboratory confirmation of Legionella infection, without pneumonia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and epidemiological supported by laboratory testing; chest imaging is important to exclude Legionnaires' disease.

laboratory: Detection of Legionella DNA by PCR in respiratory samples
Normal or mildly elevated white blood cell count
imaging: Absence of infiltrates or consolidation on chest radiograph
other: Epidemiological link to contaminated water sources (e.g., cooling towers, fountains)

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pneumonia on chest imaging
Presence of respiratory symptoms with productive cough

redFlags: Development of pneumonia or respiratory distress
Neurological deterioration or altered mental status
references: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Legionella (Legionnaires’ Disease and Pontiac Fever). CDC; 2023.
Fields BS, Benson RF, Besser RE. Legionella and Legionnaires’ disease: 25 years of investigation. Clin Microbiol Rev. 2002;15(3):506-526.
Phin N, Parry-Ford F, Harrison T, et al. Epidemiology and clinical management of Legionnaires’ disease. Lancet Infect Dis. 2014;14(10):1011-1021.
